working_title: Testing the Periodic-Table Hypothesis of Human Language
subtitle: A Predictive Comparison of Periodic and Non-Periodic Models of Cross-Linguistic Structure
promotion_target: next available paper ID after ARIS review gate
core_question: Does cross-linguistic structural diversity exhibit reproducible recurrent organization that is better modeled by a periodic geometry than by ordinary factor, hierarchical, graph/manifold, or null models?

tests: compression beyond column-wise marginal-preserving shuffle null
residual pairwise feature association beyond permutation null
stage0.claim_limit: Stage 0 tests prerequisites only; it cannot establish periodicity.

strongest_prior_art: Port et al. 2018 - Persistent Topology of Syntax
Port, Karidi & Marcolli 2022 - Topological Analysis of Syntactic Structures
Graff et al. 2025 - independent structural-feature datasets
Verkerk et al. 2025/2026 - spatiophylogenetic tests of grammatical universals
promotion_requires: Stage 1 yields an interpretable GO or defensible REFRAME result
periodic model is operationalized without post-hoc capacity advantage
family/geography-aware evaluation is included in confirmatory work
formal ARIS secondary reviewer evidence exists
closest-prior-work check finds no equivalent periodic-vs-nonperiodic predictive comparison
